summary: Harmonies is a quiet, meditative tile-stacking puzzle where you build a small hex landscape and try to satisfy several scoring conditions and animal habitat requirements at once. Turns are fast and tactile, but players work almost entirely on their own board with only light tension over which token sets remain available.
praised: Beautiful, tactile components (chunky wooden tokens, painted animal figures)
Satisfying, flexible puzzle with many viable strategies
Easy to teach, quick turns, scales well solo to 4
Rewards planning ahead without heavy analysis paralysis
criticised: Very low direct interaction, can feel like solitaire at the same table
Animal card draws add a luck element some feel undercuts the puzzle purity
End-game scoring can feel fiddly to tally
Limited long-term replay tension since opponents rarely affect your plan

interaction.kind: mostly parallel play with light drafting tension over the shared token/animal-card supply

scoring.why: Points come from multiple independent terrain-type scoring rules plus completed animal habitat cards, so the winner is whoever best balances several scoring engines rather than maximizing one.
